findings.finding: The armed count '22 of 31' overcounts what exists on disk: only 7 of 31 normative ids have any arm at HEAD. Verified by running tests/unit/test_s06_conformance.py (24 arms: OK, expected failures=5, 0.02s — all green-as-staged) and mapping its arms to ids: RED expectedFailure arms cover exactly ORC-POL-1, POL-3, POL-4/GATE-2 (one arm), DASH-1/DASH-4 (one arm), ARB-4 — 7 ids. The other 15 ids the spec counts as armed (ARB-1/2/3, DASH-2/3/5, PAUSE-1/2, POL-2/7, PROV-1, REG-1/2/3/4, via §9's C1–C14 flips column) exist only as prose rows describing controls to be written in P3 (ORC-CTRL-2 says so explicitly); repo-wide grep for ORC-* in *.py/*.sh/*.zig returns only the conformance file — no C-control is implemented anywhere. By this bundle's own rule ('an id claimed armed whose arm does not exist ... is a major'), 15 of the claimed 22 are specified, not armed. The 9-unarmed enumeration itself is correct (31 ids recounted in §1–§7 = 4+7+3+5+4+4+4; 22−7=15 planned + 7 on-disk leaves exactly GOAL-1..4, POL-5, POL-6, PAUSE-3, GATE-1, ORIENT-1 unarmed).
findings.disposition: Restate the count in three tiers: '7 armed on disk (test_s06_conformance.py), 15 specified in §9's core table and owed as batteries in P3, 9 unarmed and enumerated.' STATUS.md repeats 'armed count 22 of 31' and should carry the same correction. Refutation: if project convention counts a ratified control-table row as an arm until P3 writes it, this downgrades to a wording fix — but the convention is nowhere stated, and §0's own instrument rule ('earns its first reading only after a null control and a seeded-defect control') argues the stricter reading.
findings.verified_how: Ran the suite; read every arm's docstring and target regex; grepped the repo for any other implementation of the C-controls; recounted the 31 ids section by section; cross-checked the flips column id-by-id against the conformance file.

findings.finding: The sprint's headline consolidation — five dispatch doors become one — has no home in the spec. Roadmap §6 censused 'dispatch an execution | 5 ways' (bin/dispatch · subagent direct · runner→provider · suggest · paste-prompt) with the measured cost (159 of 364 executions skipped bin/subagent); roadmap §7 records the operator ratifying rev 2 with the parenthetical 'dispatch rewire (five doors become one)'. The spec itself never enumerates the five routes, assigns none of them a disposition, states nothing about what tools/runner does when an execution arrives by another route after pass 5, and contains no normative id requiring door collapse — grep for 'five doors', 'paste', 'another route', 'side door' returns nothing; `suggest` appears once, and only as a registration-parser call site (ORC-REG-2, spec.md:416). A literal builder executing pass 5 would rewire dispatch+subagent to read policy+registry while leaving three-plus doors open, satisfying every written id while consolidating away the exact number the sprint was ratified to fix.
findings.disposition: Add a normative id (e.g. ORC-DOOR-1) before pass 5 is minted: enumerate today's five routes, give each a disposition (route-through-bin/dispatch / refuse / retire), state tools/runner's behaviour for out-of-door arrivals (refuse, naming the one door — consistent with ORC-POL-6's unknown-model→refusal class), and arm it in §9. Refutation: any passage in the spec naming the five routes and each one's fate.
findings.verified_how: Full-text searches of the spec for door/route/suggest/paste vocabulary; cross-read roadmap §6 table and §7 ratification paragraph; confirmed ORC-GOAL-1's 'dispatches one command' is goal prose with no id-level requirement behind it.

findings.finding: (a) The operator's binding interleave ruling (roadmap §7: ordinary unrelated work must flow through the changed mechanism between passes, per pass recorded) is not accommodated anywhere in the spec — 'smoke' appears once, only as 'commit → deploy → smoke' (spec.md:504), and the P1–P5 phase plan has no inter-pass smoke slot or recording duty; STATUS.md does not mention it either. (b) Adjacent undispatchability hazard: ORC-PLAN-3 step 1 'absorbs window_policy.py, directive_policy.py', which verifiably gate every dispatch today (import window_policy at bin/dispatch:87 [88 at the 8c00704 pin] and bin/subagent:70; import directive_policy at bin/dispatch:86 [87 at pin] and tools/runner:128), while their consumers are rewired only at step 5. ABSORB's retirement timing is defined for regression scripts ('shell script retired at phase close', ORC-PLAN-4) but never for the six migration targets themselves — nothing states the modules keep being imported until pass 5 lands. Read literally, step 1 can delete both files and leave the fleet undispatchable for the whole of passes 2–5, which would also make the interleave ruling unexecutable.
findings.disposition: One amendment sentence fixes both: absorbed modules are retired when their LAST importer is rewired (pass 5 close), not at their own pass's close; and each pass's completion condition includes the recorded smoke tasks per the roadmap §7 ruling.
findings.verified_how: Import lines read at HEAD and at the 8c00704 pin (drift of −1 attributed to T805's usage-text removal, 346b5b2); spec full-text searched for smoke/interleave/between-passes; ORC-PLAN-3 and ORC-PLAN-4 read for retirement timing.

findings.finding: Pass 1 buildability (§ORC-POL alone): buildable, but a competent worker must guess at seven points. (a) Named-condition expiry resolution: no source of truth exists for 'next-ollama-quota-refresh' or 'blind-test-reveal' — who detects the condition, from what signal, is unstated; nothing today emits either event. (b) Post-lapse semantics: when an entry's expiry lapses, is the entry ignored (→ unknown model → refusal under ORC-POL-6's new rule?) or enforced stale? For oxalpha this means blind-test-reveal silently converts dial-6 into a refusal unless someone edits the file — possibly intended, nowhere stated. (c) glm/minimax/kimi are encoded twice (dial 0 AND model-level deny, same expiry string); precedence if they lapse differently is unstated. (d) 'family setting is bulk convenience' (ORC-POL-3) has no schema form — the worked example has no family appetite entry to copy. (e) Validation strictness unspecified: unknown fields refused or ignored; schema_version mismatch behaviour. (f) The override record appended to untracked/fleet-window-overrides.jsonl (ORC-POL-7) has no stated shape. (g) The reader↔block mapping is unstated — e.g. whether bin/subagent enforces cooldowns pre-launch or only bin/dispatch does.
findings.disposition: None require re-ratification; items (a)–(c) should be answered in the P2 design doc explicitly rather than by whichever choice the implementer reaches first. Refutation for (a): a passage naming the quota-refresh signal would remove guess (a).
findings.verified_how: Read §2 and §3 end-to-end against the worked example; grepped the repo for any existing quota-refresh/blind-test-reveal signal producer (none found); checked fleet-window-overrides.jsonl's existing format (free-form lines, no schema to inherit).

notes: T809 — RACE-X independent audit of S06 spec rev 2, one of three concurrent entrants (T807/T808/T809), written blind to the others. Read-only: no source, spec, or STATUS file touched. Landmark: advances L1 (hands-off orchestration) — cuts BOTH ways: rev 2's factual substrate verifies unusually cleanly (every incident number, both appetite tables, all §7c consumptions, all commit pins reproduce), which is rare and worth saying; but two majors stand between it and a build-safe ratification — the armed-count figure counts planned controls as existing arms (7 of 31 on disk, not 22), and the ratified 'five doors become one' deliverable has no normative id, no route enumeration, and no out-of-door behaviour for tools/runner, so a literal pass-5 could satisfy every written id while consolidating nothing. Milestone statement: advances L1 (hands-off orchestration) — the spec's evidence base now independently verifies, and the two amendments owed before pass 1 are named with their dispositions; what remains for L1 is ratification-with-amendments, then the six passes.
